patterns: PayrollCalculator is intended as the backend source of truth for derived payroll values.
Some exports render deductions as signed negative values while backend formulas generally use positive magnitude deductions.
Manual adjustments can enter as positive or negative; koreksi and potongan must normalize to absolute magnitude before calculation.
Excel formulas are riskier than rendered UI because a signed deduction can be accidentally subtracted twice or sign-flipped.
Payslip display often recalculates a reduced model and can drift from payroll table/export rules.
dependencies: Manual adjustment metadata and premium definitions
conflict_areas: Large dirty worktree with many frontend/backend files already changed
Multiple implementations of payroll formulas and formatting conventions
Potential mismatch between UI display, backend numeric model, Excel signed model, and tax/payslip models
Generated logs/screenshots and local artifacts mixed with source changes
constraints: Do not run broad refactors before audit findings are isolated
Document sign-convention invariants before changing formulas
Every behavioral fix needs a focused regression test
